s: Letters from the Jews of Jerusalem urging those in Egypt to keep the feast of the temple's cleansing.
Jeremiah hides the ark and the altar of incense. The author explains that he is condensing a longer history.
Heliodorus tries to rob the temple and is struck down by heavenly horsemen.
Jason buys the high priesthood and brings Greek customs into Jerusalem.
Antiochus plunders the temple. Judas Maccabeus flees to the desert.
The temple is defiled. The aged Eleazar chooses death rather than pretend to eat pork.
A mother and her seven sons are martyred for the law, trusting in the resurrection.
Judas gathers an army and defeats Nicanor.
Antiochus dies a painful death after acknowledging God.
Judas purifies the temple and wins more battles.
Lysias is defeated and makes peace with the Jews.
Judas wins more victories and offers prayers and sacrifice for the dead, that they might be freed from sin.
Antiochus Eupator invades and is forced to make peace.
Nicanor plots against Judas. The elder Razis dies rather than be captured.
Judas sees Jeremiah in a vision, receives a golden sword, and defeats Nicanor. The author ends his account.

7: The mother and her seven sons
A mother encourages her sons to die rather than break God's law, trusting that God will raise them up. It is one of the clearest Old Testament witnesses to the resurrection.
12: Judas offers prayers and sacrifice for fallen soldiers so they may be freed from sin. The Church sees here the roots of praying for the dead and the teaching on purgatory.
